/-!
# Conjecture 6.55

by V. P. Shunkov

A group $G$ of the form $G = F \leftthreetimes H$ (a semidirect product of a normal subgroup
$F$ by a subgroup $H$) is said to be a *Frobenius group with kernel $F$ and complement $H$*
if $H \cap H^g = 1$ for any $g \in G \setminus H$ and
$F \setminus \{1\} = G \setminus \bigcup_{g \in G} H^g$. Do there exist Frobenius $p$-groups?

Here a $p$-group is a group in which every element has order a power of the prime $p$
(`IsPGroup p G`, which does not assume finiteness). A finite Frobenius group has kernel and
complement of coprime orders, so a Frobenius $p$-group is necessarily infinite.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

blocks.code:
structure IsFrobeniusGroup (F H : Subgroup G) : Prop where
  /-- The kernel $F$ is normal in $G$. -/
  normal : F.Normal
  /-- $H$ is a complement of $F$, so $G = F \leftthreetimes H$. -/
  isComplement' : F.IsComplement' H
  /-- $H \cap H^g = 1$ for any $g \in G \setminus H$. -/
  inf_conj_eq_bot : ∀ g : G, g ∉ H → H ⊓ MulAut.conj g • H = ⊥
  /-- $F \setminus \{1\} = G \setminus \bigcup_{g \in G} H^g$. -/
  kernel_sdiff_one_eq :
    (F : Set G) \ {1} = Set.univ \ ⋃ g : G, ((MulAut.conj g • H : Subgroup G) : Set G)
blocks.docstring:
A group $G$ is a *Frobenius group with kernel $F$ and complement $H$* if
$G = F \leftthreetimes H$ (that is, $F$ is a normal subgroup of $G$ and $H$ is a complement of
$F$, so that $F \cap H = 1$ and $FH = G$), $H \cap H^g = 1$ for any $g \in G \setminus H$, and
$F \setminus \{1\} = G \setminus \bigcup_{g \in G} H^g$.

Here $H^g$ denotes the conjugate subgroup `MulAut.conj g • H`, i.e. $gHg^{-1}$. Since
$g \notin H$ iff $g^{-1} \notin H$ and the union ranges over all $g \in G$, this agrees with the
convention $H^g = g^{-1}Hg$. This is the literal definition from the notebook; it is
degenerately satisfied when $H = 1$ (with $F = G$) and when $H = G$ (with $F = 1$).

justification.closest_existing_considered: Subgroup.IsComplement' together with Subgroup.Normal (used as the components for G = F ⋊ H); Mathlib's external SemidirectProduct N G φ (rejected: the problem is about an internal decomposition of a given group, and the Frobenius conditions on conjugates of H must be added anyway); Subgroup.pointwiseMulAction / MulAut.conj (used for H^g).
justification.name: Kourovka.«6.55».IsFrobeniusGroup
justification.why_needed: Mathlib has no notion of Frobenius group (only Frobenius endomorphisms/numbers), and FormalConjecturesForMathlib has none either. The predicate transcribes the notebook's own definition of 'Frobenius group with kernel F and complement H' clause by clause, for a possibly infinite group G. Two API tests (`isFrobeniusGroup_top_bot`, `isFrobeniusGroup_bot_top`) are proved.

blocks.text:
/--
A group $G$ is a *Frobenius group with kernel $F$ and complement $H$* if
$G = F \leftthreetimes H$ (that is, $F$ is a normal subgroup of $G$ and $H$ is a complement of
$F$, so that $F \cap H = 1$ and $FH = G$), $H \cap H^g = 1$ for any $g \in G \setminus H$, and
$F \setminus \{1\} = G \setminus \bigcup_{g \in G} H^g$.

Here $H^g$ denotes the conjugate subgroup `MulAut.conj g • H`, i.e. $gHg^{-1}$. Since
$g \notin H$ iff $g^{-1} \notin H$ and the union ranges over all $g \in G$, this agrees with the
convention $H^g = g^{-1}Hg$. This is the literal definition from the notebook; it is
degenerately satisfied when $H = 1$ (with $F = G$) and when $H = G$ (with $F = 1$).
-/
structure IsFrobeniusGroup (F H : Subgroup G) : Prop where
  /-- The kernel $F$ is normal in $G$. -/
  normal : F.Normal
  /-- $H$ is a complement of $F$, so $G = F \leftthreetimes H$. -/
  isComplement' : F.IsComplement' H
  /-- $H \cap H^g = 1$ for any $g \in G \setminus H$. -/
  inf_conj_eq_bot : ∀ g : G, g ∉ H → H ⊓ MulAut.conj g • H = ⊥
  /-- $F \setminus \{1\} = G \setminus \bigcup_{g \in G} H^g$. -/
  kernel_sdiff_one_eq :
    (F : Set G) \ {1} = Set.univ \ ⋃ g : G, ((MulAut.conj g • H : Subgroup G) : Set G)

@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isFrobeniusGroup_top_bot : IsFrobeniusGroup (⊤ : Subgroup G) ⊥ where
  normal := inferInstance
  isComplement' := Subgroup.isComplement'_top_bot
  inf_conj_eq_bot _ _ := bot_inf_eq _
  kernel_sdiff_one_eq := by simp
blocks.docstring: The degenerate case $H = 1$, $F = G$ satisfies the literal definition.

@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«6.55» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ (p : ℕ) (G : Type) (_ : Group G) (F H : Subgroup G),
      p.Prime ∧ IsPGroup p G ∧ IsFrobeniusGroup F H ∧ H ≠ ⊥ ∧ H ≠ ⊤ := by
  sorry
blocks.docstring:
Do there exist Frobenius $p$-groups?

That is, is there a prime $p$ and a group $G$ in which every element has order a power of $p$
such that $G$ is a Frobenius group with some kernel $F$ and complement $H$? The complement $H$
is required to be a nontrivial proper subgroup, $1 \ne H \ne G$; this is the standard
nontriviality assumption on Frobenius groups, and without it the question has a trivial
positive answer (see `isFrobeniusGroup_top_bot` and `isFrobeniusGroup_bot_top`).

claims.decomposer_note: Existential yes/no question: is there a prime p and a group G in which every element has p-power order (necessarily infinite, since a finite Frobenius group has coprime kernel and complement) that is a Frobenius group in the statement's sense (G = F ⋊ H with F normal, F ∩ H = 1, FH = G, H ∩ H^g = 1 for g ∉ H, and F∖{1} = G ∖ ⋃_g H^g); the literal definition is degenerately satisfied by H = 1 (F = G) or H = G (F = 1), so the standard nontriviality 1 ≠ H ≠ G must be imposed to avoid a trivial positive answer, and p should be quantified existentially, with `answer(True)` meaning such groups exist.
claims.reviewer_why: All eight candidates state the same proposition: answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ prime p, group G with IsPGroup p G (elementwise p-power order, no finiteness), subgroups F H with F normal, F.IsComplement' H (F ∩ H = 1, FH = G, i.e. G = F ⋊ H), H ∩ H^g = 1 for g ∉ H, F \ {1} = G \ ⋃ H^g, and the standard nontriviality H ≠ ⊥ ∧ H ≠ ⊤. I verified in Mathlib that IsComplement' is bijectivity of F × H → G, that MulAut.conj g • H = gHg⁻¹ (equivalent to g⁻¹Hg here since g ∉ H is inversion-closed and the union is over all g), and that IsPGroup is ∀ g, ∃ k, g^p^k = 1. c02 chosen as base: literal bespoke structure with per-field docstrings, two proved `category test` lemmas showing the degenerate (⊤,⊥)/(⊥,⊤) cases (justifying the added nontriviality), and a docstring explaining the added hypothesis. Minor docstring edit only (conjugation convention note). c04's extra `Infinite G` is redundant (no finite Frobenius p-group exists) but a departure from the source, so not used; c03/c05/c07's inlined forms are equally faithful but less readable.

decomposition_objections.text: None. The single-slot table is correct: the question is an existential yes/no question, p should be existential, and the literal definition needs the standard nontriviality 1 ≠ H ≠ G to avoid a trivial positive answer (both degenerate cases are proved as tests in the file).

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 6.55

by V. P. Shunkov

A group $G$ of the form $G = F \leftthreetimes H$ (a semidirect product of a normal subgroup
$F$ by a subgroup $H$) is said to be a *Frobenius group with kernel $F$ and complement $H$*
if $H \cap H^g = 1$ for any $g \in G \setminus H$ and
$F \setminus \{1\} = G \setminus \bigcup_{g \in G} H^g$. Do there exist Frobenius $p$-groups?

Here a $p$-group is a group in which every element has order a power of the prime $p$
(`IsPGroup p G`, which does not assume finiteness). A finite Frobenius group has kernel and
complement of coprime orders, so a Frobenius $p$-group is necessarily infinite.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

open scoped Pointwise

namespace Kourovka.«6.55»

variable {G : Type*} [Group G]

/--
A group $G$ is a *Frobenius group with kernel $F$ and complement $H$* if
$G = F \leftthreetimes H$ (that is, $F$ is a normal subgroup of $G$ and $H$ is a complement of
$F$, so that $F \cap H = 1$ and $FH = G$), $H \cap H^g = 1$ for any $g \in G \setminus H$, and
$F \setminus \{1\} = G \setminus \bigcup_{g \in G} H^g$.

Here $H^g$ denotes the conjugate subgroup `MulAut.conj g • H`, i.e. $gHg^{-1}$. Since
$g \notin H$ iff $g^{-1} \notin H$ and the union ranges over all $g \in G$, this agrees with the
convention $H^g = g^{-1}Hg$. This is the literal definition from the notebook; it is
degenerately satisfied when $H = 1$ (with $F = G$) and when $H = G$ (with $F = 1$).
-/
structure IsFrobeniusGroup (F H : Subgroup G) : Prop where
  /-- The kernel $F$ is normal in $G$. -/
  normal : F.Normal
  /-- $H$ is a complement of $F$, so $G = F \leftthreetimes H$. -/
  isComplement' : F.IsComplement' H
  /-- $H \cap H^g = 1$ for any $g \in G \setminus H$. -/
  inf_conj_eq_bot : ∀ g : G, g ∉ H → H ⊓ MulAut.conj g • H = ⊥
  /-- $F \setminus \{1\} = G \setminus \bigcup_{g \in G} H^g$. -/
  kernel_sdiff_one_eq :
    (F : Set G) \ {1} = Set.univ \ ⋃ g : G, ((MulAut.conj g • H : Subgroup G) : Set G)

/-- The degenerate case $H = 1$, $F = G$ satisfies the literal definition. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isFrobeniusGroup_top_bot : IsFrobeniusGroup (⊤ : Subgroup G) ⊥ where
  normal := inferInstance
  isComplement' := Subgroup.isComplement'_top_bot
  inf_conj_eq_bot _ _ := bot_inf_eq _
  kernel_sdiff_one_eq := by simp

/-- The degenerate case $H = G$, $F = 1$ satisfies the literal definition. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isFrobeniusGroup_bot_top : IsFrobeniusGroup (⊥ : Subgroup G) ⊤ where
  normal := inferInstance
  isComplement' := Subgroup.isComplement'_bot_top
  inf_conj_eq_bot g hg := (hg (Subgroup.mem_top g)).elim
  kernel_sdiff_one_eq := by simp [Set.iUnion_const]

/--
Do there exist Frobenius $p$-groups?

That is, is there a prime $p$ and a group $G$ in which every element has order a power of $p$
such that $G$ is a Frobenius group with some kernel $F$ and complement $H$? The complement $H$
is required to be a nontrivial proper subgroup, $1 \ne H \ne G$; this is the standard
nontriviality assumption on Frobenius groups, and without it the question has a trivial
positive answer (see `isFrobeniusGroup_top_bot` and `isFrobeniusGroup_bot_top`).
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«6.55» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ (p : ℕ) (G : Type) (_ : Group G) (F H : Subgroup G),
      p.Prime ∧ IsPGroup p G ∧ IsFrobeniusGroup F H ∧ H ≠ ⊥ ∧ H ≠ ⊤ := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«6.55»

items: Conjugate subgroup H^g is modelled as `MulAut.conj g • H` (= gHg⁻¹, verified: x ∈ MulAut.conj g • H ↔ g⁻¹ x g ∈ H). The notebook's H^g is usually g⁻¹Hg, but both the condition 'for all g ∉ H' and the union over all g ∈ G are invariant under g ↦ g⁻¹, so the two conventions give the same predicate.
G = F ⋊ H (internal semidirect product) is modelled as `F.Normal ∧ F.IsComplement' H`, i.e. F normal and (f, h) ↦ f * h bijective, which is exactly F ∩ H = 1 and FH = G.
H ∩ H^g = 1 is stated as `H ⊓ MulAut.conj g • H = ⊥` at the subgroup level; F \ {1} = G \ ⋃ H^g is stated verbatim as an equation of sets in G.

The nontriviality 1 ≠ H ≠ G is placed in the theorem statement (`H ≠ ⊥ ∧ H ≠ ⊤`) rather than in the definition, so the definition matches the notebook literally and the added assumption is visible; two `category test` lemmas prove that the literal definition is degenerately satisfied by (F,H) = (⊤,⊥) and (⊥,⊤), documenting why the exclusion is necessary. H ≠ ⊤ forces F ≠ ⊥ and H ≠ ⊥ forces F ≠ ⊤ via the complement condition, so no extra condition on F is needed.

'p-group' is read as: p is a prime and every element of G has order a power of p (`p.Prime ∧ IsPGroup p G`), the standard infinite-group meaning; p is quantified existentially, as the notes require. Finiteness is not assumed (a finite Frobenius p-group cannot exist).
The group G is quantified over `Type` (universe 0), following the other Kourovka files (1_40, 1_74, 19_25, 20_76).

reviewer_notes: Faithfulness points checked: (1) p is existential and answer(True) means a Frobenius p-group exists for some prime p; (2) p.Prime is required (otherwise e.g. p = 0/1 or composite p breaks the meaning); (3) no finiteness imposed, matching the notebook (Shunkov's school works with infinite groups; a finite Frobenius p-group cannot exist since |H| divides |F|-1); (4) the notebook's literal definition is degenerately satisfied by H = 1 or H = G — proven as test lemmas in the file — so the standard 1 ≠ H ≠ G is imposed at theorem level, visibly, as the decomposition table requires; the definition itself remains a verbatim transcription. Conjugation convention gHg⁻¹ vs g⁻¹Hg is immaterial here. Final file compiles with only the `declaration uses 'sorry'` warning.
